title: Wisconsin Democratic Primary Debate for Governor

topics.label: The state of the race
topics.blurb: Crowley's re-entry, Hong's DSA membership, Barnes' 2022 loss, and whether single-digit polling ends a candidacy.
topics.anchor: It is fair to say that this race has been chaotic

topics.label: Policing and public safety
topics.blurb: The Madison police shooting of Corey Ruys, body cameras, and whether any of them would cut police budgets.
topics.anchor: Last week, a Madison police officer shot and killed a man

topics.label: Affordability and the failed tax deal
topics.blurb: The Evers–Republican rebate deal that died in the state Senate, and who would have signed it.
topics.anchor: Let's move on to the economy tonight

topics.label: The budget surplus
topics.blurb: Return the projected $2.5 billion to taxpayers, or spend it — and on what.
topics.anchor: Congressman Tom Tiffany is campaigning on the fact that he would return the entire surplus

topics.label: Taxing the wealthy
topics.blurb: Each candidate's specific income threshold and rate, pressed for numbers.
topics.anchor: We did bring up taxes, so let's move on to taxes

topics.label: Property taxes
topics.blurb: School referenda, the two-thirds funding commitment, and shared revenue.

topics.label: School vouchers
topics.blurb: Whether to end, cap or keep the nation's oldest school choice program — the sharpest split of the night.
topics.anchor: We brought up vouchers, so let's talk about vouchers right now

topics.label: AI data centers
topics.blurb: Moratorium, pause, or guardrails, with 76% of Wisconsinites telling Marquette the costs outweigh the benefits.

topics.label: Governing a divided legislature
topics.blurb: What survives if Republicans keep the legislature.
topics.anchor: Everything you've talked about tonight relies on a democratically controlled legislature

topics.label: Closing statements
topics.blurb: Thirty seconds each, in an order drawn at random.
topics.anchor: it is now time for closing statements

handVotes.question: Would you sign legislation requiring all police and sheriff's departments in Wisconsin to have body cameras?
Would you have signed the Evers–Republican tax relief deal into law if it had passed?
Would you commit to an across-the-board property tax decrease?

quotes.quote: Well, thanks so much for the question and thanks so much for having me. There's not a single person on this stage who's united all shades of blue of the Democratic Party as I have before. Now that race in 2022, it was the closest US Senate race in the state in over one hundred years. It was the closest challenge to any incumbent across the entire country. No incumbent lost statewide. Now while DC insiders like Chuck Schumer didn't see the race as winnable, Republican billionaires certainly did.
quotes.fullAnswer: Well, thanks so much for the question and thanks so much for having me. There's not a single person on this stage who's united all shades of blue of the Democratic Party as I have before. Now that race in 2022, it was the closest US Senate race in the state in over one hundred years. It was the closest challenge to any incumbent across the entire country. No incumbent lost statewide. Now while DC insiders like Chuck Schumer didn't see the race as winnable, Republican billionaires certainly did. They spent over $50,000,000 to defeat me, and I only lost by one point, 26,000 votes. Now I can tell you, having been the only person on this stage who's actually won statewide in 2018 when we kicked Scott Walker out of office for good, that race was also decided by one point. Now I've been on both sides of the coin, and you learn a whole lot more when you lose. When you win, you think you did everything right. But when you come up that short, you have a whole lot of time to think about the things that went wrong. You learn about the devastating impact of big money in politics. You also learn about how low Republicans can get, and I can tell you right now we have the resources and we have the support to get it done and on the terms of governor Evers, I have zero interest in upholding the status quo. I have zero interest in being the establishment candidate. That is the difference right here on the stage because I am pushing the envelope to make sure that we are as bold as we can possibly be in the Donald Trump era because that's what people have been calling for Democrats to be all along. We have not truly met the moment.
quotes.question: Mr Barnes, you were once seen as the clear front runner in this race. You previously lost a statewide election for US Senate when the field cleared for you. In fact, last year, the Milwaukee Courier said we need a candidate who can unite this state and win. Mandela Barnes already showed us he can't, and Governor Tony Evers recently endorsed David Crowley over you. So why should primary voters now trust you that you can win statewide this time?

quotes.quote: Well, here's what I would tell you is I don't think primary voters have been paying much attention until the last two weeks and all the upheaval that you have seen. This is what I find when I am going out around the state is that, and this has been verified by polls that was done here by my alma mater at Marquette, because about half the people at this point haven't made a decision. And so that is a lane that's opening up. The challenge that I have had from day one is not that anybody thinks I'm unqualified for the office. I am I served as the top appointee to Governor Evers.
quotes.fullAnswer: Well, here's what I would tell you is I don't think primary voters have been paying much attention until the last two weeks and all the upheaval that you have seen. This is what I find when I am going out around the state is that, and this has been verified by polls that was done here by my alma mater at Marquette, because about half the people at this point haven't made a decision. And so that is a lane that's opening up. The challenge that I have had from day one is not that anybody thinks I'm unqualified for the office. I am I served as the top appointee to Governor Evers. We created the largest budget surplus in state history. We increased the rainy day fund. We got millions billions of dollars out to family farms, to small businesses, to renters who needed it during COVID. So all of that stuff puts me in good stead. The challenge I have had is that people don't know me as well as they know some other candidates around the state. And so what I have found in recent days is that the disruption, the upheaval, somebody putting their thumb on the scale, it has gotten people much more engaged and much more interested in this race. And day by day I am feeling that momentum and I'm feeling people who want somebody who can beat Tom Tiffany in the fall and who can hit the ground running on day one. And I I will put my qualifications on those issues up against anybody in this race.
quotes.question: Mister Brennan and miss Roys, you are both polling in the single digits and have been since the start of this race. At this point, are primary voters wasting their vote on a vote for you, mister Brennan?

quotes.quote: Well, first and foremost, thank you for having us, but I was never born into the establishment. I was actually born into struggle. I grew up in the 53206 zip code where I had to work extremely hard for everything that I have, and so I'm not here to protect the establishment. I'm here to deliver real results for Wisconsinites all over our states. And, you know, I like to make decisions based off of the data, based off of facts. And we learned ever since that day that a lot of things have changed, and we were going off of false data.
quotes.fullAnswer: Well, first and foremost, thank you for having us, but I was never born into the establishment. I was actually born into struggle. And so we know that the stakes are too high this upcoming election, and that's why I got back into this race. And I'm honored to not only have the endorsement of governor Tony Evers, but lay labor unions and leaders all across this state who believe in my leadership, and I'm looking forward to delivering for all of Wisconsin.
quotes.question: Mr Crowley, three weeks ago you dropped out of this race saying you couldn't see a path to victory. Eleven days ago, the primary upended when Sara Rodriguez dropped out and you made the unprecedented move of reentering the race with an immediate endorsement from Governor Tony Evers. Since then, you have been linked to a social media account that includes offensive posts. You've said you didn't write any of those, and some have accused you of being the latest prop for the Democratic establishment. So are you and why should voters now trust your judgment and ability to win?

quotes.quote: Well, first, thank you so much to the team at WISN, the Marquette University for hosting this important debate. I do not support the full platform of the National DSA, and I'm not endorsed by DSA National. What democratic socialism is is a form of government that puts working class people first, that puts work first. The policies that we have been working on, permanent affordability, has broad bipartisan support in every corner of the state.
quotes.fullAnswer: Well, first, thank you so much to the team at WISN, the Marquette University for hosting this important debate. I do not support the full platform of the National DSA, and I'm not endorsed by DSA National. What democratic socialism is is a form of government that puts working class people first, that puts work first. The policies that we have been working on, permanent affordability, has broad bipartisan support in every corner of the state. Well, things like fully funding our public schools, ensuring that we are doing right by our kids and cutting property taxes. Taxing the ultra wealthy and mega corporations, ensuring that we can invest in free childcare, and that everyone has access to affordable housing. And we are the only campaign to support a moratorium on AI data centers, and we have found broad bipartisan support. I am looking forward to helping the Democrats become the big tent party that they've aimed to be for many years.
quotes.question: Miss Hong, you are the Democratic Socialist who is leading in all the polls, yet some Democrats are attempting to stop you from winning, fearful that you cannot beat Republican Tom Tiffany. Just this weekend, the co chair of the Democratic Socialists of America, which you are a member, reaffirmed the DSA's position of abolishing the senate, prisons, and replacing the presidency and the supreme court as we know it. Do you fully back the DSA platform, and why should primary voters trust your judgment and your ability to win statewide?

quotes.quote: If you want the best public schools in the nation for your children, if you want to open up the state's health care plan so that everyone can buy in and we can lower costs for all Wisconsinites, if you want a candidate who is gonna stand up and fight Donald Trump and bring an end to this authoritarian regime, then you should vote for me. I am the candidate in this race that brings the most experience in and around state government with ten years of service in the legislature and the only one who served on the state budget committee.
quotes.fullAnswer: If you want the best public schools in the nation for your children, if you want to open up the state's health care plan so that everyone can buy in and we can lower costs for all Wisconsinites, if you want a candidate who is gonna stand up and fight Donald Trump and bring an end to this authoritarian regime, then you should vote for me. I am the candidate in this race that brings the most experience in and around state government with ten years of service in the legislature and the only one who served on the state budget committee. I've also been an executive in the private and nonprofit sectors, and for over twenty years, I've been the candidate that has turned progressive ideas, like the kind that all of us have on this stage, into law. That kind of experience is absolutely essential, and voters need to think about not just who can beat Tom Tiffany, although that is important, Not just who can deliver a democratic legislature, although that is vitally important, but who can actually do the job on day one. And I am proud to have earned by far the most endorsements of any candidate in this race, including the most endorsements in Milwaukee County, the most, largest labor union endorsement with WEAC, the state teachers union, and, the endorsement of former lieutenant governor Barbara Lawton.
quotes.question: Mister Brennan, thank you. Miss Roys, you are continuing to poll in the single digits as well. At this point, are primary voters wasting their vote on a vote for you?

quotes.quote: First of all, we should all be very disturbed by what we saw in those images, what we saw in the video. And we should fight as hard as we possibly can as a state, as a people, as a society, to make sure that never happens again. And body cameras, of course, are the norm. It should be the norm. And I wish that the Madison Police Department did have those body cameras. So of course, I would not sign a budget that reduced funding because obviously that police department needs the funding to have body cameras.

quotes.question: Mister Barnes, you have previously shown support for reducing police funding and abolishing ICE. Following the Madison shooting, you said you were deeply disturbed and pained. Would you sign a bill or budget that cuts funding for police departments?

quotes.quote: Of course I wouldn't. And I think as others have said here, there's been a generation of disinvestment and a broken system between the state, the broken partnership between state and local government. So we need to make sure that we're robustly funding that. It has been demonstrated. This hundred and fifteen year old contract that we have had between state and local government worked pretty well for the first eighty years. And then the Republicans just turned off the spigot and stopped funding local government. So we need to make sure we do that.
quotes.fullAnswer: Of course I wouldn't. And I think as others have said here, there's been a generation of disinvestment and a broken system between the state, the broken partnership between state and local government. So we need to make sure that we're robustly funding that. It has been demonstrated. This hundred and fifteen year old contract that we have had between state and local government worked pretty well for the first eighty years. And then the Republicans just turned off the spigot and stopped funding local government. So we need to make sure we do that. On the larger issue of criminal justice reform, we need to look a little bit to our neighbors to the West. In Minnesota, they spend about $215 per capita on criminal justice in that state. They they're about the same size. They have about the same crime rate. We have about three times as many people incarcerated. In Wisconsin, we spend about $315 per capita on that. As a long term target, spending that $600,000,000 difference that they spend on other things in Minnesota, spending those on early childhood, on K-twelve education, on other programs in Wisconsin, that would be the kind of investment over the long term that would put us in better stead and keep us from having fewer of these incidents. Because they should outrage all of us, but there are ways that we can make a difference on those by spending our money differently.
quotes.question: Mr. Brennan, after the shooting in Madison, you are also calling for investigation. Would you sign a bill or a budget that cuts funding for police departments?

quotes.quote: No. Did not rush to judgment with my comments. My thoughts and prayers are not just with Corey and his family and friends, but with the entire Madison community and everybody who's been affected and retraumatized by this. Again, we have seen these types of incidents happening here locally with Jacob Blake, as well as George Floyd in Minnesota. And so it's extremely important that we have transparency. We cannot defund the police. We should be investing in public safety, and that doesn't mean more money to police officers. That's like investing in in in in in systems like the community violence interruption.
quotes.fullAnswer: No. Did not rush to judgment with my comments. My thoughts and prayers are not just with Corey and his family and friends, but with the entire Madison community and everybody who's been affected and retraumatized by this. Again, we have seen these types of incidents happening here locally with Jacob Blake, as well as George Floyd in Minnesota. And so it's extremely important that we have transparency. We cannot defund the police. We should be investing in public safety, and that doesn't mean more money to police officers. That's like investing in in in in in systems like the community violence interruption. Milwaukee County, we have been a leader in actually helping to reduce violent crime here in Milwaukee County, working directly hand in hand with not just police departments, but also community organizations. And so we have to focus on not just investing upstream, but making sure we wrap around services around families so that they don't have to go down the road of criminality in the first place.
quotes.question: Brennan, thank you. Mr. Crowley, without first seeing any video, you said that you were horrified by the reports of the shooting and immediately pointed to other police shootings in Kenosha and Minneapolis. Did you rush to judgment with your comments, and would you sign a bill or budget that cuts funding for police departments?

quotes.quote: The governor cannot defund police, and I'm not here to govern by slogan. I'm here to make sure that I am the governor that is most serious about public safety, That means investing in the things that we know prevent crime and getting resources to victims and ensuring that the people who are incarcerated and the folks who are working in our prisons are able to live a life of dignity and work with dignity.
quotes.fullAnswer: The governor cannot defund police, and I'm not here to govern by slogan. I'm here to make sure that I am the governor that is most serious about public safety, That means investing in the things that we know prevent crime and getting resources to victims and ensuring that the people who are incarcerated and the folks who are working in our prisons are able to live a life of dignity and work with dignity. I think it's important that we invest in communities, including our public schools, out of of school programs, and mental health resources, and attacking the opioid, epidemic. These these are things that are proven to prevent crime, and this is what will help to make sure that we have a government that is serious about public safety.
quotes.question: You have also called to defund and abolish police before while saying your ideal world is one without prisons. Would you sign a bill or budget that cuts funding for police departments? No. No, why not?

quotes.quote: No, but I think we need to actually fund local communities so that we can do evidence based programs that actually reduce and prevent crime. At the end of the day, I'm a mom and stepmom of five. I want my kids and every kid to be safe in our communities, and I want law enforcement officers to be safe in our communities.
quotes.fullAnswer: No, but I think we need to actually fund local communities so that we can do evidence based programs that actually reduce and prevent crime. At the end of the day, I'm a mom and stepmom of five. I want my kids and every kid to be safe in our communities, and I want law enforcement officers to be safe in our communities. That means that we have to invest in proven strategies that actually do that, unlike what Republicans like Tom Tiffany have done, which is cut funding to local governments, and take away local control so that communities don't have the resources to be able to actually solve these problems effectively. I am really proud, as the only attorney on this stage, to be someone that has fought for and passed criminal justice reforms to make us more safe and more just. I have taken on racial disparities in areas from health to criminal justice, and I believe that Wisconsin can be a place where everyone has the freedom to thrive, but not if we aren't willing to tackle these really tough issues.
quotes.question: Miss Roys, after the Madison shooting, you said we do not have to accept this as inevitable. We can create a more fair, safe world. Would you sign a bill or budget that cuts funding for police departments?

I think folks understand here in the state of Wisconsin when you have divided government, it can be a bit chaotic. Were there things in this bill that I did not like? Absolutely. I love the fact that we were going to give relief into our schools and property tax relief, and there are other things in this bill that I didn't like. At the end of the day, we know that there are many Wisconsin families who are desperate. We should be focusing on how we lift them up and not playing politics.

quotes.question: Thank you. Mr. Crowley, you're the only one who raised your hand to sign the deal. Why would you have signed it into law?

quotes.quote: Because at the end of the day, my job is to be a responsible steward of taxpayer dollars, and this would have created a $2,900,000,000 deficit down the road, which our schools and our health care system and our local governments cannot afford. It also would have spent the surplus before it even materialized. Look at what is happening with the economy.
quotes.fullAnswer: Because at the end of the day, my job is to be a responsible steward of taxpayer dollars, and this would have created a $2,900,000,000 deficit down the road, which our schools and our health care system and our local governments cannot afford. It also would have spent the surplus before it even materialized. Look at what is happening with the economy. When we are spending money that we do not yet have and spending it in ways that do not actually help us solve the long term problem of getting more money into our public schools, giving property tax relief to property taxpayers, and making sure that we have a more fair, just tax system, All we are doing is throwing that money away on a political gimmick that was frankly cooked up by Robin Vos as he sees the blue wave coming and wanted to do anything that he could to either protect his members from losing their seats and run away from their terrible record on public education, which Tom Tiffany is partially responsible for.
quotes.question: Miss Roys, you were one of the 15 Democratic senators who helped kill the deal. Why?

quotes.quote: Well, let's first talk about how we got here. Now, the reason there is a surplus is because Republicans in the legislature have failed the people of Wisconsin. Our school districts are going to referendum every single year just to keep the lights on. And we also see gaps in health care because we are one of 10 states that has yet to extend our excuse me, expand our Medicaid program under the Affordable Care Act. We are in a world of trouble and Robin Vos has never been a good negotiating partner.
